html: Lab alum Kyle and Stelios, together with Liane Young, published a paper in Futures on the sociodemographic predictors of self- and other-oriented future concern!

Led by lab volunteer Duncan Ward, we published a new paper in the Journal of Environmental Psychology, investigating how specific human value profiles emerge in young adults in Europe, and what their impact is on perceptions of climate change. This was Duncan's fist publication! Congrats Duncan!

Led by collaborator Trystan Loustau, a new paper was published in Political Psychology supervised by Stelios examining misperceptions of dynamic norms relevant to intergroup attitudes by US partisans.
Stelios supervised a collaboration between multiple institutions on how the diversity of social networks relates to indicators of well-being, published in Self and Identity

Lab alum Kyle and Stelios together with a larger research team published a paper in the Journal of Community and Applied Social Psychology on the impact of impartial intergeenerational beneficence and intergenerational concern on career choice!

Stelios received the SAGE Emerging Scholar Award by the Society for Personality and Social Psychology. This distinction recognizes outstanding achievements by early-career PhD scholars in social and personality psychology. Stelios was recognized for his contributions to research.
Lab alum Kyle and Stelios together with the research team of Rare published a paper in Climatic Change on audience demand for climate content in entertainment media (spoiler alert, it is high!).

Stelios was part of a research team who published a study in Journal of Community & Applied Social Psychology investigating how cultural humility could help reduce the negative effect of collective narcissism on support for multiculturalism.
Together with Tyler DesRoches and Joan McGregor Stelios published a paper in the Canadian Journal of Philosophy on how ecological humility could coincide with arguments for geoengineering.

Stelios and Kyle were part of a collaboration resulting in a paper published in Group Processes and Intergroup Relations showing that Republicans underestimate the degree to which other Republicans are not feeling negative towards an increasingly racially diverse U.S. population.
Kyle and Stelios together with collaborators from Boston College published an article in Political Psychology on ideological differences in the moral circle!
Stelios and Jin were awarded an Institute for Social Science Research Seed Grant to develop online interventions to increase ecological humility! Go team!
Jin an APA Division 34 (Society for Environmental Population and Conservation Psychology) Research Grant to conduct two studies on threat perceptions and climate justice! Congrats Jin!
Jin received a CAP-LTR grant to conduct research on how well-being and life satisfaction change over time in the Phoenix Valley! Congrats Jin!

Jin published her first first-authored paper! The paper was a fully lab-led investigation (including Kyle and Stelios) seeking to determine the moral standing of future generations relative to other entities! The paper was published at Group Processes and Intergroup Relations.
Stelios was part of a collaborative investigation investigating how similarity to animals correlates with worldview defense. The paper was published at Group Processes and Intergroup Relations.
Stelios and Jin wrote a piece for the outlet The Conversation for their paper on nature connectedness and well-being across the world! The piece received 16,00 reads across the world!
Kyle and Stelios published a paper at Group Processes and Intergroup Relations on how scientific journals supporting presidential candidates influences trust in science.
Kyle and Stelios were part of an investigation on preferences for sustainability practices on the Moon! The paper was published in the journal Space Policy!

A paper led by collaborator Dr. Deborah Wu, focusing on disparities in the experiences of graduate students in psychology and how they correlate with intentions to stay in academia was published in Analyses of Social Issues and Public Policy.

Led by volunteer research assistant Grace Bauer mentored by Kyle and Stelios, the lab published a paper in the British Journal of Social Psychology, on how concern for future generations predicts present day extreme acts of altruism (e.g., donating an organ),
In collaboration with ASU Farm, the lab received a seed grant from the Lincoln Center for Applied Ethics to evaluate the impact of volunteering at agricultural spaces on campus!

A paper led by volunteer Grace Bauer, mentored by Kyle and Stelios was published in the British Journal of Social Psychology, on how concern for future generations predicts present day extreme acts of altruism (e.g., donating an organ).

Kyle, Jin and Stelios together with ASU collaborator Tyler DesRoches published a paper introducing a reliable and psychometrically valid instrument capturing ecological humility in the Journal of Environmental Psychology!

Jin's first official paper is published! Check out one of the largest to-date multinational investigations of the impact of nature connectedness on mental health at the Journal of Environmental Psychology!

A collaborative team led by Trystan Loustau including Stelios published an article in Social Cognition investigating how social ties influence the perceived motives of actors engaging in prosociality!

Another PNAS Nexus piece is out! Led by Kyle, this piece explores how cognitive and empathy-related constructs predict (effective and impartial) prosociality in the general population, effective altruists, and anonymous organ donors.
The IDEA Lab attended SPSP 2026 in Chicago! We were featured in a total of 15 presentations!

The IDEA lab was covered twice in public media! Kyle gave an interview to a KJZZ about our obituaries paper, whereas Stelios was featured on a short radio segment by the Yale Program on Climate Change Communication.
A large collaborative megastudy, that Stelios participated in on behavioral interventions for increasing climate advocacy was published in PNAS Nexus!
Kyle and Stelios co-wrote with collaborators Deborah Wu and Sylvia Perry on how well-being fluctuates during democratic backsliding in Advances in Psychology.
Kearney, Kyle and Stelios co-wrote a piece on how expansion of our ingroup can fuel distant altruism. This piece was published in Social and Personality Psychology Compass

Stelios was a member of a large team that published a paper on a cross-national investigation of the relationship between conspiracy beliefs and dispositional individual victimhood tendencies at the Journal of European Social Psychology.

Stelios and a team of co-authors across several institutions published a paper on how worldviews shifted during the first year of the COVID-19 pandemic at the Journal of Social and Political Psychology.

Kyle and Stelios published a paper that maps the prevalence of (high) support for initiatives protecting future generations, as well as intervention tools for increasing support in the United States, at Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin.
Stelios was part of a team that published a paper on how cultural humility can help reduce intergroup conflict at the Journal of Applied Social Psychology.
Kyle and Stelios co-lead a project mapping and increasing intergenerational stewardship beliefs at Scientific Reports.
Kyle published the first paper of his dissertation on the moral architecture of extraordinary and effective altruism at PNAS Nexus! Congrats Kyle!

Stelios was part of a large consortium that published a paper in Science Communication finding that social media are the most used sources of science information in most countries, except those with democratic-corporatist media systems where news media tend to be used more widely.

Stelios, Kyle, and collaborators from the Center for the Science and the Imagination received a small grant to study how an educational program focusing on future thinking can help veterans transition back to civilian life.

Kyle and Stelios together with collaborators from Boston College and Cornell University published a paper that expands the better than average effect for ratings of virtue in the British Journal of Social Psychology.
Kyle and Stelios co-led a multi-country team which published a paper on cross-national variation in moral expansiveness to nature and humans in the Journal of Environmental Psychology.
Stelios was part of a multi-country team which published a paper in Social Psychological and Personality Science, on the impact of macro-economic inequality on national stereotypes.

Stelios, Kyle, and collaborators from the Center for the Science and the Imagination received a small grant to study how educational workshops can increase imaginative capacity and future thinking in undergraduate students.

Kyle and Stelios were part of a multi-person research team which published a paper in the Journal of Individual Differences, on the association between self-reports of intergenerational concern and personal well-being!

Kyle and Stelios were part of a 5-person research team (together with researchers from Boston College and Michigan State University) which published a paper at Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, on the values that are reflected in obituaries!

Kyle, Zhaoquan and Stelios published a paper at Journal of Environmental Psychology which expands past work on responsibility to future generations by investigating the psychological mechanism in Europe and determining how perceptions of severe weather events influence responsibility. This was also Zhaoquan's 1st paper!
The TISP team led by collaborator Viktoria Cologna published a paper on extreme weather attribution and its impact on climate attitudes in Nature Climate Change!
Collaborator Luca Versteegen and Stelios published a paper on interventions that seek to reduce reaction to racial threat from White conservatives in the US in the journal Political Behavior!
Kyle, Stelios and collaborator Dr. Deborah Wu received an Institute for Social Science Research Seed Grant ($8k)!
Jin received a Graduate College Enrichment Fellowship! Congratulations Jin!
Stelios and collaborators Hallie Eakin and Sarah Porter received a $130k grant to study water conservation in Scottsdale, AZ!
Stelios and Kyle published a paper on interventions that increase moral concern for future generations at the British Journal of Social Psychology!
Christina Jinhee Capozzoli joined the IDEA lab! Welcome Jin! We are delighted to work with you!
Stelios and Gregg Sparkman published an article in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences on anthropogenic climate change belief consensus in Christian religious leaders.
The IDEA Lab attended SPSP 2025 in Denver! We were featured in seven posters and 3 talks! Denver was cold, but we brought the heat!
With collaborators from Boston College, Stelios published a multi-study paper on the benefits of intellectual humility in Personality and Individual Differences
Stelios was part of a many-labs study on trust in science that was published in Nature Human Behaviour.
Stelios was featured on the Climate Change & Happiness podcast.
Kyle and Stelios published an article in Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin on the principle of impartial intergenerational beneficence.
The IDEA Lab website is created.
